replication_status: exact_code_rerun: the authors' aggte(dynamic, -12..12) path is reproduced by hand-pooled did cells (event_structure.verified); the published figure is graphical only
published_source: Figure 4: event-study coefficients shown graphically only (aggte dynamic -12..12 of out0, es_graph()); published figure in the article (Marketing Science 42(6), Figure 4) is graphical only. authors_rerun_post_summary is the overall ATT of that aggregation from the authors' code re-run (did 2.5.1).
notes: Figure 4: dynamic aggregation (-12..+12 months, reference -1) of the same att_gt object as T8_cs_senti0. Callaway-Sant'Anna specification as published: did::att_gt(yname, tname = exp_ymfe, idname = hotel_id, gname = first_response_ymfe [0 = never], xformla = ~1, control_group = 'notyettreated', allow_unbalanced_panel = TRUE; did defaults base_period = 'varying', est_method = 'dr', multiplier bootstrap SE) on the hotel x year-month panel the authors build in r_replication_code.R (lines 191-194); outcome senti_score_k = round(mean(senti_score_k), 4) over the hotel's sentiment-scored reviews in the month (built from reviews with non-missing senti_score_0). Panel rebuilt verbatim from rating_data.dta in 01_explore_prepare.R (row counts equal the published Observations). published_coef is the authors' CS ATT, not a TWFE; run_spec.R's TWFE/BJS on this panel are unweighted hotel-month regressions that the paper does not report. run_spec.R runs did on this panel with the relaxed size guard (csa_max_cells/csa_max_obs, Nov 1) and the same unbalanced-panel cells and not-yet-treated controls as the authors; the authors' CS calls were also re-run separately (logs/authors_csa_results.csv). Nov 2 audit: event_structure records the published structure (single horizons -12..12, reference -1, endpoint bins for the TWFE counterpart); replaces the Nov 1 legacy re-normalization, which coincided with it for this paper.
csa_guard_note: relaxed CSA size guard (CSA_MAX_CELLS=20000, CSA_MAX_OBS=4e6) as in the overnight relaxed-guard queue, Nov 1

event_structure.source: r_replication_code.R es_graph() (line 22-23): aggte(attgt, type = 'dynamic', min_e = -12, max_e = 12, na.rm = TRUE, bstrap = FALSE, cband = FALSE) of att_gt(gname = first_response_ymfe, tname = exp_ymfe, control_group = 'notyettreated', allow_unbalanced_panel = TRUE, base_period default 'varying'); Figure 4 line 192; event time e = exp_ymfe - first_response_ymfe in year-months; published bins = single horizons -12..12 (e = -1 estimated under the varying base; post horizons relative to g-1).
event_structure.verified: Pipeline index: exp_ymfe 1..112 with no gaps in this sample, so rel = t - g equals the authors' e for every treated-hotel row (0 mismatches); earliest cohort month 4 > first sample month, so no pre-sample adopters (1 treated hotel has no hotel-month before its cohort and is always treated in sample, as in the authors' att_gt). Hand-computed did cells (cohort means of the hotels observed in each month, not-yet-treated controls, varying base) pooled within each single-horizon bin with cohort-size weights reproduce the authors' aggte path e = -12..12 (did 2.5.1 re-run of their code, logs/authors_csa_dynamic_T8_senti0.csv) to 1.1e-16; post horizons under the pipeline's universal base are identical (1.1e-16). Post summary (equal-weight mean of horizons 0..12 = aggte dynamic overall ATT) = 0.034191; pre summary -12..-2: -0.000890 with the authors' varying base vs 0.008067 with the universal base the pipeline uses (the published figure's pre path is the varying-base one). The figure is graphical only (no printed coefficients). The paper has no TWFE event study; the TWFE counterpart on this panel estimates the same single-horizon indicators with endpoint bins <= -13 and >= 13 (identical to the legacy coding; relative times outside the window are not pooled with the reference). Same sample as the authors (row count equals the published Observations).

csa_weights_note: Nov 2: the published CSA comes from R did (or staggered, whose estimates did reproduces), which weights cells by fixed cohort shares; Hull's DiD-averaging weights cells by treated-observation counts. 'did' reproduces the published number (main analysis, option B); the strict-Hull run (CSA_STRICT_HULL=1, option A) ignores this field.
